rows.notes: Calendar-2025 production (100% basis) = 1.35 Mt of spodumene concentrates: IGO (S1, from 6.16 Mt ore at 1.9% Li2O) and Tianqi annual report (S2: 1.35 Mt = 1.30 Mt chemical grade + 0.05 Mt technical grade) agree. This is CY2025 and replaces the earlier IGO FY25 (Jul24-Jun25) 1,479 kt figure; ~1.35 Mt is ~9% below FY25 (the Tianqi/Shanghai Securities snippet 'up 9.8%' is ambiguous and not used). Norm = 1,350,000 t x 6.0% Li2O x 2.473 = 200,313 t LCE (81,000 t Li2O). Grade basis: chemical grade is SC6.0 (S3 TRS: H2-2025 forecast in SC6.0) and technical grade is 5-7.2% (S3), so 6% for all 1.35 Mt is an assumption (technical grade is only 50 kt, 4% of output); no single stated average grade. Built capacity: Tianqi AR says the five operating concentrators total ~2.14 Mt/yr (S2, includes CGP3 whose first on-spec chemical-grade product came 30 Jan 2026 and which is to finish ramp-up during 2026, hence ref year 2026). capacity_norm = 2,140,000 x 0.06 x 2.473 = 317,533 t LCE (SC6.0 basis, same assumption). CONFLICT: Albemarle TRS (earlier row text) forecasts 1.8-2.0 Mtpa after CGP3 'over the next two years'; the earlier 2.0 Mt / 2027 value is superseded by the company-built figure (the lead may prefer the range). IGO FY25 1,479 kt kept in history only here. [production_year 2025 = calendar year.]

PRODUCTION (replaces the earlier FY25 sales-derived 428 kt): MinRes Q4 FY26 report, Wodgina table is on a '50% attributable basis' (S5). FY26 (Jul 2025-Jun 2026) attributable produced = 345k dmt mixed grade = 317k dmt SC6-equivalent; 100% = 2 x 317k = 634,000 t SC6-eq. (= 690k dmt at ~5.5%). Norm = 634,000 x 6% x 2.473 = 94,073 t LCE. Cross-check: 690k dmt is ~92% of the 750 kt nameplate, consistent with the 50% reading; the SC6-eq production equals SC6-eq sales (both 317k) by coincidence of the report. FY25 alternative (comparative column of the same table, PDF page 6): attributable produced SC6 231k -> 100% = 462,000 t SC6-eq -> 68,552 t LCE (FY25 sales SC6 214k, the earlier row's basis). production_year 2026 = FY26 (year to 30 Jun 2026); the table values are read from the PDF page image/text. CAPACITY (was null): MinRes site page: three processing trains, ~750,000 t/yr spodumene concentrate at 5.5% Li2O (S4, undated page; 100% basis; MinRes Q4 FY26 says all three trains operate from Q1 FY27). capacity_norm = 750,000 x 5.5% x 2.473 = 102,011 t LCE. A search-result summary quoted 820,000 t at 5.5% for the same page; the page as fetched says 750,000 (used). ref year 2026 = access-year fallback. POSCO deal to take 30% of MinRes' 50% (completion expected 1H FY27) does not change the site capacity.

PRODUCTION (replaces the FY25 shipment-derived 406 kt): MinRes Q4 FY26 report, Mt Marion table is on a '50% attributable basis, unless otherwise indicated' (S6). FY26 attributable produced = 316k dmt mixed grade = 227k dmt SC6-eq; 100% = 2 x 227k = 454,000 t SC6-eq. Norm = 454,000 x 6% x 2.473 = 67,365 t LCE. Basis caveat: the same table labels the Sales rows '(51%)' (FY26 sales SC6 242k), so MinRes' share might be 51% rather than 50% in places; with 51% the 100% production would be ~445 kt SC6-eq (66,100 t LCE) - difference <2%. Ownership in this database is 50/50 with Ganfeng. FY25 alternative (comparative column): attributable produced SC6 180k -> 360,000 t SC6-eq -> 53,417 t LCE. CAPACITY: Ganfeng AR (S10): flotation upgrade planned 2026, completed end-2027, after which Mt Marion capacity is expected to be 600,000 t of 6% concentrate; MinRes took FID in May 2026 on a flotation plant plus underground (A$490M, 100% basis, FY27-FY28, S6 text). So 600,000 t SC6, ref year 2027, replaces the Mysteel reported value; norm = 600,000 x 6% x 2.473 = 89,028 t LCE. Current (pre-upgrade) capacity not stated in an opened source (FY26 100% output of 454 kt SC6-eq is the running rate).

FY26 (year to 30 Jun 2026). Wesfarmers release (S7, opened, verbatim): 'Spodumene concentrate production of 209kt was above both guidance and nameplate capacity' - the release itself does not state the basis. S&P Global (S8, search-result text only, page 403) says 209,000 t is WesCEF's 50% share, up 44.1% from ~145 kt in FY25; this is consistent with 209 kt being above the 50% share of 380 kt nameplate (190 kt) but would be ~55% of the 100% nameplate if it were 100%, which could not be 'above nameplate'. 100% production = 2 x 209 kt = 418,000 t (DERIVED, reported tier). Grade is NOT stated for current output: norm uses the design/PFS concentrate grade 5.5% Li2O (S9 Wood Mackenzie summary, reported tier): 418,000 x 5.5% x 2.473 = 56,854 t LCE. If the true grade is 5.0% the value is 51,700; if 6.0% 62,000. Row confidence kept <=0.5. FY25 comparison from the earlier note (not re-verified): ~145 kt WesCEF share -> ~290 kt at 100%. Nameplate 380 kt (100%) to 760 kt after the July 2026 FID is already in the row.

2025 production 'more than 31,000 t LCE' (+29% vs 2024) per Panorama Minero (trade press, 4 Oct 2026), which attributes its figures to the latest lithium market report of Argentina's National Mining Secretariat (the report itself was not opened). Recorded as 31,000 t (a lower bound: 'more than'). Unit LCE, so norm = 31,000. Rio Tinto no longer reports Fenix separately (see Olaroz row). Cross-check: Rio Tinto 2025 group lithium output 57 kt LCE on a Rio-share basis (Q4 2025 production release summary), of which Arcadium assets only from March 2025; the Diario Financiero figure of 68 kt LCE for Rio's Argentine operations (earlier row note) is of unclear basis and is not reconciled.

2025 production 34,000 t (LCE basis per the article's national table, utilization >85% of installed capacity) per Panorama Minero citing Argentina's National Mining Secretariat market report (report not opened). Risk: the same article gives Cauchari-Olaroz as 'more than 34,000 t LCE' (>80% utilization) which equals the company's 34,100 t, so the Olaroz 34,000 could be a mix-up with Cauchari-Olaroz; the different utilization percentages (85% vs 80%) and 34,000/0.85 = 40,000 t installed (vs 42,500 t Stage 2 nameplate) argue for a genuine separate value. Not corroborated by Rio Tinto (no separate disclosure). 100% basis (Rio Tinto 66.5% / Toyota Tsusho 25% / JEMSE 8.5%).

Second, independent confirmation from the Ganfeng 2025 annual report: Cauchari-Olaroz produced 34,100 t lithium carbonate in 2025 (S11; same as Lithium Argentina's 34,100 t), phase-1 design capacity 40,000 t LCE/yr (S12; confirms the previously derived 40,000), Ganfeng holds 46.67% and control (S12b). Ganfeng AR also states a phase-2 planned capacity of 45,000 t LCE/yr (environmental permit applied Dec 2025) - undated, still excluded; whether 45 kt is an increment or the new total remains unstated. 2026 guidance 35-40 kt carbonate (S11 text).

Upgrades the earlier reported-tier production: Ganfeng 2025 annual report states Goulamina produced 336,600 t (dry) of concentrate in full-year 2025 (S13), matching the MiningDataOnline 337 kt aggregator figure; Phase I planned capacity 506,000 t concentrate (S14). Grade: not stated in the annual report; the Stage 1 DFS nameplate is 506,000 t/yr of 6% Li2O spodumene concentrate (SC6) (S15, SMM). Norm = 336,600 x 6% x 2.473 = 49,945 t LCE; capacity_norm = 506,000 x 6% x 2.473 = 75,080 t LCE. If actual shipped grade is ~5.5% the production norm is ~45,800 t LCE (an upper-bound caveat: grade of actual shipments not confirmed). Ganfeng holds 65% (AR line 1751-1753 context: 'holds 65%'). Compare USGS Mali 2025e 9,400 t Li = 50,036 t LCE: the 49,945 t LCE here is ~100% of it (Bougouni is additional, see its row: >45,000 t of concentrate produced by early Nov 2025 per Kodal-related press, not an annual figure, not recorded). [lead] capacity_ref_year = publication-year fallback.

FY26 (year to 30 Jun 2026) production 197,967 dmt confirmed in Elevra's Form 6-K (S18, now a confirmed quote; previously search-summary only). Concentrate grade produced FY26 = 5.0% (FY25 5.3%) per the 6-K operating table (S19; unit % Li2O by convention, label not spelled out in the extract). Norm = 197,967 x 5.0% x 2.473 = 24,479 t LCE (Li2O content 9,898 t). FY25 alternative: 204,858 dmt x 5.3% x 2.473 = 26,850 t LCE. Sales FY26 were lower (181,494 dmt per a search summary, not used). 100% basis (Elevra wholly owns NAL).

2025 figure is SALES, used as a production proxy: AMG sold 69,180 dmt of lithium concentrates in 2025 (-22% vs 88,966 dmt in 2024), hit by an equipment failure in Q2 2025 and poor ore quality in Q4 (S20; Mibra is AMG's only concentrate source). Production itself not published in the opened pages. Grade of AMG concentrate is not stated in the opened sources; norm uses the Brazilian national average concentrate grade 5.50% Li2O reported by ANM for 2025 (S21, search-result text, reported tier): 69,180 x 5.5% x 2.473 = 9,410 t LCE. Low confidence (proxy volume + borrowed grade). Brazil total per ANM (S21): 306,514 t of spodumene concentrate at 5.50% = 16,858 t Li2O = 41,692 t LCE, so Sigma 183 kt + Mibra ~69 kt leaves ~54 kt of 2025 output for CBL (inferred by difference only; not recorded in the CBL row).

production_norm only: 183,000 t (reported tier, earlier SC005 row) x 5.5% x 2.473 = 24,891 t LCE. Grade 5.5% = product name 'SC5.5' in this row and the ANM national average 5.50% (S21, reported snippet); no Sigma document stating the 2025 average grade was opened (Sigma FY2025 results release opened: gives 4Q25+1Q26 sales and 240,000 t/12-month guidance but no 2025 production). Production itself remains unconfirmed (183 kt is from a call summary); a Sigma 2025 figure would also be consistent with the ANM national total (see Mibra row).

Resolves the capacity conflict (Asian Metal 300,000 vs Newsday 350,000): Yahua's 2025 annual report states both phases were completed in 2024 and the mine now processes 2.3 Mt/yr of ore and produces 350,000 t/yr of lithium concentrate (S22, lines 570-572); a second passage (line 1206) says Kamativi concentrate 'reached design output in H2 2025'. installed_as_of 2025-12-31 is therefore derived (reached in H2 2025). The earlier capacity_by_year_json {2024: 50,000} (phase 1 only) is now stale: the AR says phase 1 was commissioned end-2023 and phase 2 end-2024 but gives no per-phase tonnages, so no new steps were added. Product grade is not stated -> no norm. NO 2025 production figure is in the annual report (searched for production/sales volume tables: only lithium salts are tabulated). Ownership per AR subsidiary table: Yahua group holds 85.00% of Kamativi Mining Company (KMC, 'acquired'); the 15% partner (Denfold, per earlier reported-tier note) is not named in the AR text read.

Company annual report (Shengxin Lithium Energy SZSE 002240, English name Chengxin Lithium; Max Mind Zimbabwe is its subsidiary) states that 5 of the 40 mining rights are in production at 990,000 t/yr ore and can yield ~290,000 t/yr of lithium concentrate, commissioned May 2023 (S23). This replaces the USGS 300,000 t. PRODUCTION: the AR reports only a COMBINED figure for its mine subsidiaries - lithium concentrate output of 299,800 t in 2025 (+4.82%), covering Sabi Star (Zimbabwe) and Yelonggou (Sichuan, 405 kt/yr ore, ~75 kt/yr concentrate) (S24); no per-mine split is given, so production is left null here and the China Yelonggou row is not modified. Subsidiary revenue 2025: Max Mind Zimbabwe RMB 1,033.9M vs Aoyinuo (Yelonggou) RMB 365.3M (AR subsidiary table) - a revenue split only, not a tonnage split. Zimbabwe national context: MMCZ/Reuters spodumene exports 1.128 Mt in 2025 vs 1.014 Mt in 2024 (S27, exports not production).

Capacity 600,000 t now confirmed by the company's own annual report: Bikita 2 Mt/yr spodumene flotation line yields ~300,000 t/yr spodumene concentrate and the 2 Mt/yr petalite line ~300,000 t/yr chemical-grade petalite concentrate (S25) - matches USGS. Mixed spodumene (~6% Li2O) and petalite (~3-4%) products, so no LCE norm. No 2025 Bikita concentrate output is disclosed in the AR (only lithium salt output of 37,408 t in 2025 for the whole group, which is mostly from purchased feed).

Sinomine 2025 AR (S26, quote: 'Tanco 矿山现有 18 万吨/年处理能力的锂辉石采选系统'): Tanco's spodumene mining and processing system currently has 180,000 t/yr ore-processing capacity; a 1 Mt/yr mining and processing expansion was approved by the board in Feb 2023 (CAD 176M, AR line ~5987, status not confirmed). Not entered as capacity because the row's capacity unit is concentrate tonnes and a 'feed' tonnage would corrupt the LCE normalisation. No lithium concentrate output disclosed; Tanco's contribution to Canada's USGS 5,600 t Li is therefore uncovered.
